title: Quantum Information Geometry of Multicomponent Superconducting Fluctuation Transport
authors: Zi-Ting Sun, Ying-Ming Xie, Naoto Nagaosa
abstract: Quantum geometry underlies many electronic responses, but its transport signatures have so far been established mainly for pure single-particle Bloch states. Whether collective many-body fluctuations possess a measurable quantum geometry remains largely unexplored. Here we show that superconducting fluctuation transport provides a direct probe of quantum information geometry in collective many-body matter. Starting from a multicomponent time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau theory in the Gaussian fluctuation regime, we identify the equilibrium density matrix of fluctuating Cooper pairs as the static pair propagator, which defines a positive mixed-state manifold in momentum space. The geometry of this manifold is directly measurable through paraconductivity: the longitudinal paraconductivity is governed by the quantum Fisher information of superconducting fluctuation modes, while the fluctuational anomalous Hall effect is governed by the mean Uhlmann curvature, the mixed-state counterpart of Berry curvature. This correspondence further yields geometric bounds between these two transport components, with no direct analogue in normal electronic transport. Applied to chiral superconducting fluctuations in quarter-metal systems motivated by rhombohedral multilayer graphene, a symmetry-allowed Lifshitz invariant generates finite mean Uhlmann curvature and logarithmically enhances the anomalous Hall conductivity above the critical temperature. Our results establish collective superconducting fluctuations as an experimentally accessible transport probe of mixed-state quantum information geometry.
summary: The paper establishes that collective superconducting fluctuations act as a unique probe of mixed-state quantum information geometry. By analyzing the paraconductivity components—specifically relating longitudinal conductivity to Quantum Fisher Information and anomalous Hall effect to mean Uhlmann Curvature—the authors demonstrate a deep geometric connection previously unseen in normal metals. This provides a powerful theoretical framework for understanding fluctuation transport near superconducting transitions.
main_problem: To determine if collective many-body superconducting fluctuations possess a measurable quantum geometry and how this geometry manifests in transport properties.
main_result: Superconducting fluctuation transport provides a direct, experimentally accessible probe of mixed-state quantum information geometry via the relationship between paraconductivity components and geometric tensors like the Quantum Fisher Information and mean Uhlmann Curvature.
method: The analysis uses time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau theory in the Gaussian fluctuation regime to derive kinetic equations for the pairing fluctuation density matrix, linking transport coefficients to quantum information metrics.
model_or_system: The system is a multicomponent superconductor exhibiting fluctuations above the critical temperature ($T > T_c$), modeled using a time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau (TDGL) theory. The core object of study is the equilibrium density matrix of fluctuating Cooper pairs, which defines a mixed-state manifold.
key_observables: Longitudinal paraconductivity ($\sigma_{L}$), fluctuational anomalous Hall conductivity ($\sigma_{	ext{para}}^H$), Quantum Fisher Information (QFI), and mean Uhlmann Curvature (MUC).
important_parameters: Temperature relative to $T_c$ ($r \propto (T - T_c)/T_c$), fluctuation parameters ($\gamma_\pm, \lambda$), and the ratio of kinetic coefficients ($\Xi''/\Xi'$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is performed in the Gaussian fluctuation regime, utilizing low-frequency/long-wavelength approximations for the inverse propagator, and assuming a specific relaxation structure for the kinetic coefficient.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate how longitudinal paraconductivity relates to QFI ($J_x \propto F_{xx}$) and anomalous Hall conductivity relates to MUC ($J_y \propto U_{xy}$), showing characteristic divergences near $T_c$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the link between quantum geometry and transport in general (Chunk 1) to deriving the kinetic equation for the pairing fluctuation density matrix (Chunk 2, Chunk 5). It then analyzes critical asymptotics by examining the soft branch of the inverse propagator (Chunk 6), culminating in specific applications to chiral superconductors (Chunk 3).
why_interesting: This work bridges fundamental concepts from quantum information theory (mixed-state geometry) directly into measurable condensed matter transport phenomena, providing a novel diagnostic tool for strongly correlated superconducting states.
